# Fairstay Month End Close (`fairstay-month-end-close`)

Month-end close checks for nursing homes: trial balance out of balance, intercompany that does not net, suspense and unapplied cash balances, missing recurring accruals, late close tasks, big month-over-month swings and per-patient-day costs outside their usual range. Resident names in suspense detail are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Month End Close never posts journal entries to the general ledger.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-month-end-close demo
npx -y fairstay-month-end-close mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

A fictional Cedar Hollow March 2026 close (operating company and property company), checked on 6 April. Planted:

- The OpCo trial balance is out by 1200.
- Due-from PropCo is 95000, but PropCo's due-to is only 90000.
- Suspense holds 106310, and unapplied cash holds 6450 in three resident payments, the oldest 82 days old.
- No contract therapy was booked for March.
- Pharmacy is 11.14 per patient day, below its usual 20 to 32, and agency staffing more than doubled.
- The payroll accrual task is two days late, and ancillary accruals are due tomorrow.

Residents named in the unapplied cash detail are in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `close_check` | Run the month-end close checks, blocking problems first. | runs |
| `close_write_report` | Write close.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and close.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/close). | runs |
| `close_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `close_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `close_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `close_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `journal_post` | Fairstay Month End Close never posts journal entries to the general ledger. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `close_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tb` (required) | Trial balance under --root: entity, account, name, this month's activity, last month's activity, ending balance |
| `tasks` | Optional close checklist under --root: task, owner, due date, done date |
| `suspense` | Optional suspense and unapplied cash detail under --root: account, date, amount, resident, memo |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: patient_days, swing_pct, swing_min, accruals, ppd ranges |
| `as_of` | Close date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-month-end-close inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Trial balance (`tb`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `entity` | text | Entity, Company, Facility, Building |
| `account` (required) | text | Account, Account Number, GL Account, Acct, Account # |
| `name` | text | Name, Account Name, Description, Account Description |
| `activity` | amount | Activity, Current Month, This Month, Net Change, Period Activity |
| `prior_activity` | amount | Prior Activity, Prior Month, Last Month |
| `balance` (required) | amount | Balance, Ending Balance, YTD Balance, Closing Balance |

### Close checklist (`tasks`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `task` (required) | text | Task, Step, Close Task, Description |
| `owner` | text | Owner, Assigned To, Preparer |
| `due` | date | Due, Due Date, Day Due |
| `done_on` | date | Done, Done On, Completed, Completed On |

### Suspense detail (`suspense`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `account` (required) | text | Account, Account Number, GL Account, Acct, Account # |
| `date` | date | Date, Posted, Entry Date |
| `amount` | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `memo` | text (masked) | Memo, Description, Reference |

## Settings file (`close_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `patient_days` | Patient days this month, for per-patient-day checks |
| `swing_pct` | Flag month-over-month moves above this percent (default 25) |
| `swing_min` | ...and at least this amount (default 5000) |
| `accruals` | Accounts that need activity every month |
| `ppd` | Usual per-patient-day ranges |

## Memory

`close_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `close_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `swing_explanation` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-month-end-close": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-month-end-close",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-month-end-close -- npx -y fairstay-month-end-close mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-month-end-close tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-month-end-close sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-month-end-close inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-month-end-close call close_check '{"tb":"<tb>"}'
fairstay-month-end-close eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-month-end-close demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
